# ω-Regular Expressions

An **$\omega$-regular expression** denotes a language of infinite words as a finite union
$$ \bigcup_{i=1}^{n} U_i\, V_i^{\omega}, $$
where each $U_i,V_i$ is an ordinary regular language of *finite* words and $V_i$ contains no empty word. The **Büchi–expression equivalence theorem** says these denote exactly the Büchi-recognisable ($\omega$-regular) languages.

Two features make the $U\,V^{\omega}$ shape the right normal form:

- the $\omega$-power $V^{\omega}$ supplies the *infinite* behaviour by repeating finite blocks from $V$ forever;
- the finite prefix $U$ absorbs a *transient* that need not follow the periodic pattern.

Below are two languages over $\Sigma=\{a,b\}$, each shown as an expression **and** as its Büchi automaton. Membership of an ultimately-periodic word $u\cdot v^{\omega}$ is decided by looking only at the period $v$.

---

```{=html}
<script>
(function(){
  const parse=s=>s.trim().split(/[\s,]+/).filter(x=>x.length);
  const A2 = `<svg viewBox="0 0 240 120" style="width:100%;height:auto" role="img">
    <defs><marker id="nb17m" markerWidth="9" markerHeight="9" refX="8" refY="3" orient="auto"><path d="M0,0 L0,6 L8,3 z" fill="#303036"/></marker></defs>
    <line x1="4" y1="60" x2="34" y2="60" stroke="#303036" stroke-width="2" marker-end="url(#nb17m)"/>
    <path d="M 50 44 C 30 6, 90 6, 70 44" stroke="#303036" stroke-width="2" fill="none" marker-end="url(#nb17m)"/><text x="60" y="8" text-anchor="middle" font-weight="700">b</text>
    <path d="M 78 50 C 110 34, 138 34, 170 50" stroke="#303036" stroke-width="2" fill="none" marker-end="url(#nb17m)"/><text x="124" y="34" text-anchor="middle" font-weight="700">a</text>
    <path d="M 170 72 C 138 88, 110 88, 78 72" stroke="#303036" stroke-width="2" fill="none" marker-end="url(#nb17m)"/><text x="124" y="100" text-anchor="middle" font-weight="700">b</text>
    <path d="M 190 44 C 170 6, 230 6, 210 44" stroke="#303036" stroke-width="2" fill="none" marker-end="url(#nb17m)"/><text x="200" y="8" text-anchor="middle" font-weight="700">a</text>
    <g transform="translate(60,60)"><circle r="18" fill="#e8e8f0" stroke="#999" stroke-width="2"/><text text-anchor="middle" dy="4" font-weight="700">q</text></g>
    <g transform="translate(200,60)"><circle r="22" fill="#d4f7ef" stroke="#2ec4b6" stroke-width="1.5"/><circle r="17" fill="#d4f7ef" stroke="#2ec4b6" stroke-width="2"/><text text-anchor="middle" dy="4" font-weight="700">f</text></g>
  </svg>`;
  const A1 = `<svg viewBox="0 0 240 120" style="width:100%;height:auto" role="img">
    <defs><marker id="nb17n" markerWidth="9" markerHeight="9" refX="8" refY="3" orient="auto"><path d="M0,0 L0,6 L8,3 z" fill="#303036"/></marker></defs>
    <line x1="4" y1="60" x2="34" y2="60" stroke="#303036" stroke-width="2" marker-end="url(#nb17n)"/>
    <path d="M 50 44 C 30 6, 90 6, 70 44" stroke="#303036" stroke-width="2" fill="none" marker-end="url(#nb17n)"/><text x="60" y="8" text-anchor="middle" font-weight="700">a,b</text>
    <path d="M 78 60 L 170 60" stroke="#303036" stroke-width="2" marker-end="url(#nb17n)"/><text x="124" y="50" text-anchor="middle" font-weight="700">b (guess)</text>
    <path d="M 190 44 C 170 6, 230 6, 210 44" stroke="#303036" stroke-width="2" fill="none" marker-end="url(#nb17n)"/><text x="200" y="8" text-anchor="middle" font-weight="700">b</text>
    <g transform="translate(60,60)"><circle r="18" fill="#e8e8f0" stroke="#999" stroke-width="2"/><text text-anchor="middle" dy="4" font-weight="700">p</text></g>
    <g transform="translate(200,60)"><circle r="22" fill="#d4f7ef" stroke="#2ec4b6" stroke-width="1.5"/><circle r="17" fill="#d4f7ef" stroke="#2ec4b6" stroke-width="2"/><text text-anchor="middle" dy="4" font-weight="700">g</text></g>
  </svg>`;
  const LANGS=[
    {expr:'L&#8322; = (a+b)*&#183;a&#183;((a+b)*&#183;a)&#969;', svg:A2,
     note:'A run visits the accepting state f exactly at positions labelled a. So f recurs infinitely often iff a occurs infinitely often.',
     accepts:v=>v.includes('a'),
     why:v=>v.includes('a')?'the period contains an a, so a occurs infinitely often':'the period has no a, so after the stem only finitely many a’s remain'},
    {expr:'L&#8321; = (a+b)*&#183;b&#969;', svg:A1,
     note:'The automaton reads any prefix in p, nondeterministically guesses the last a, and enters g where only b is allowed. It accepts iff eventually the word is all b.',
     accepts:v=>!v.includes('a'),
     why:v=>!v.includes('a')?'the period is all b, so from the stem onward no a appears':'the period contains an a, so a recurs infinitely often — the guess into g always fails later'}
  ];
  function run(){
    const L=LANGS[+document.getElementById('nb17-lang').value];
    const u=parse(document.getElementById('nb17-u').value), v=parse(document.getElementById('nb17-v').value);
    document.getElementById('nb17-expr').innerHTML=L.expr;
    document.getElementById('nb17-svg').innerHTML=L.svg;
    document.getElementById('nb17-note').textContent=L.note;
    const strip=document.getElementById('nb17-strip'), verdict=document.getElementById('nb17-verdict');
    strip.innerHTML=''; verdict.innerHTML='';
    if(!v.length){verdict.innerHTML="<div class='verdict-box verdict-fail'>Period cannot be empty.</div>";return;}
    for(const s of u.concat(v)) if(!['a','b'].includes(s)){verdict.innerHTML=`<div class='verdict-box verdict-fail'>Unknown symbol "${s}". Alphabet is {a,b}.</div>`;return;}
    const seq=u.concat(...Array(3).fill(v));
    seq.forEach((s,i)=>{const inTail=i>=u.length; const posInV=(i-u.length)%v.length;
      const d=document.createElement('span'); d.className='tok'+(i<u.length?' stem':'')+((inTail&&L.accepts(v)&&s==='a')?' hit':''); d.textContent=s; strip.appendChild(d);});
    const ok=L.accepts(v);
    verdict.innerHTML=`<div class="verdict-box ${ok?'verdict-pass':'verdict-fail'}"><strong>&alpha; ${ok?'&isin;':'&notin;'} ${L.expr.split(' = ')[0]}</strong> — ${L.why(v)}.</div>`;
  }
  document.getElementById('nb17-lang').addEventListener('change',run);
  document.getElementById('nb17-run').addEventListener('click',run);
  ['nb17-u','nb17-v'].forEach(id=>document.getElementById(id).addEventListener('keyup',e=>{if(e.key==='Enter')run();}));
  run();
})();
</script>
```

Notice $L_1$ and $L_2$ are **complements** of each other: every $\omega$-word has either finitely or infinitely many $a$'s. That $L_1$ is again $\omega$-regular is a special case of the general complementation theorem — proved algebraically in Chapter 4 (**[Notebook 24](24-saturation-complement.qmd)**).
